# Reviewing ccmorph

ccmorph holds every profile's credentials and routes every Claude Code session
on this Mac, so a bug here is a session reaching the wrong backend, leaking a
credential, or losing the user's choice.

## Output

- Open the review with one count line, exactly like `N Important, M notes`.
- Every finding cites `file:line` on the diff's head plus the input that breaks it; no `file:line` → not a finding.
- Only Important blocks: a real bug, data loss, credential or security exposure, or one of the kinds below.

## What failure looks like here

- **Backend, identity or credential env leaking into a launch or `claude auth` call** — a provider, identity or token name left set — `example: 4b80ca8 fix(launch): clear more provider, identity and credential env names`; also `e95b598 fix(auth): scrub CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR around claude auth calls`.
- **A nested launch inheriting the parent session's state** — `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` or another child-session var — `example: c3ebf44 fix(launch): a nested launch does not inherit claude --bare's CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`.
- **One reader skipping the merged view** — a `$ccmorphUnset` tombstone that counts in one settings path and not another — `example: 189b398 fix(settings): every layer reader honours $ccmorphUnset`; also `9bce711 fix(settings): ignore a shared policy's tombstones in the readers too`.
- **The user's choice silently overruled** — a picked model or saved setting ignored, or an older model substituted — `example: 1e7a17c fix(launch): stop the role default overwriting a picked model`; also `9963261 fix(shim): never fall back to an older model`.
- **Signals or exit status lost between launcher and claude** — TERM/HUP not forwarded, the tty or the exit code dropped — `example: 63ba318 fix(launch): forward TERM and HUP from the launcher to claude`.
- **A shim rewrite corrupting the forwarded body** — UTF-8/CJK, surrogates, signed thinking, opaque tool input — `example: 5e9d09e fix(shim): keep CJK as UTF-8 when stripping metadata and repairing references`; also `52d918f fix(gateway): keep signed thinking and opaque tool input in sanitation`.
- **A loopback hop or catalogue read with no bound** — ambient proxy, cross-origin redirect, no deadline, unbounded body — `example: bcd9d26 fix(adapter,shim): loopback hops bypass ambient http_proxy`; also `b1dc252 fix(shim): end catalogue reads at their deadline`.
- **A runtime floor or upstream CLI contract assumed** — a Python 3.9+ API on the 3.8 floor, a flag Claude Code does not accept — `example: e14eecb fix: drop 3.9-only str.removeprefix/removesuffix from shipped helpers`; also `d50fe3c revert(rc): remote-control rejects --effort, so effort= took every bridge down`.
- **A redaction helper whose error path returns the secret it was meant to hide** — a parse failure that falls back to the raw value, so a proxy password holding a `^`, a bare `%` or a space is printed, or a `/`, `?` or `#` inside the password ends the authority mid-secret and the password's head prints as the host, or a digit or empty password head that Go accepts as a port, so the parse succeeds and the path still carries the secret, or the cut those fixes made, read from the other end, takes an `@` in a path or query for the userinfo's close, so the segment behind it prints as a host that does not exist (`https://gw.example.com/v1/@team` → `https://team`; 2026-11-04: behind a port-bearing gateway the guard still cut whenever the segment's tail parsed as host:port, `https://gw.example.com:8443/v1/@team:8080` → `https://team:8080`) — `example: #47 fix(adapter): --print-config redacts a proxy URL Go cannot parse`; also `#65 fix(adapter): --print-config redacts a proxy password that ends the authority`, `#139 fix(profile): a path or query @ names no host (2026-11-03)`, `#164 fix(profile): a path or query @ names no host, whatever the tail (2026-11-04)`. Seen 2× (2026-11-03, 2026-11-04).
- **A deadline only some documented paths arm** — a bound armed for `--model` but not `--auto`, though the launcher always passes `--auto` and adds `--model` only for a picked model — `example: #47 fix(adapter): --auto without --model is bounded by the select deadline`.
- **An observer still looking for the child process after the component moved in-process** — doctor kept scanning the snapshot for a `shim` child after the shim became a server inside the adapter process, so a healthy session read as a fault and the port its base_url pointed at was never checked; the ps fixture kept faking the old child shape, so the suite could not see it — `example: #49 fix(doctor): running-adapter reports the adapter's own in-process shim listener (in-process since #40)`.
- **A fix wired into the entry point the default path no longer takes** — the pre-shard move was started with `go moveFlatRows()` in the standalone shim executable's `Main`, but the adapter serves the shim in-process through `shim.Listen` and never enters `Main` (the shim moved in-process in #40), so only a `CCMORPH_SHIM_HOOKS` build or a manual `ccmorph-core shim report` ran it and a store still holding flat rows kept making every quota read open every one of them (2026-11-13, `69f8302`); kin to the observer kind one entry up (`#49`), both mistakes being about where the shim now lives — `example: 69f8302 fix(shim): finish the pre-shard usage move at every adapter start`; also `#513 fix(adapter): the pre-shard move starts with the in-process shim`.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-13).
- **A test that cannot fail** — inherits the suite's env, scratch home gone, asserts nothing ran — `example: 438e66f test(launch): make the fork_forward stderr test able to fail`; also `#141 test(zsh): an empty env-key list fails the suite at the door` (2026-11-03: the empty-list guard's `return 1` sat inside an anonymous function, so it only left that function — sourcing continued, the arrays stayed empty, and a core answering nothing left the suite green). Seen 1× (2026-11-03).
- **A new writer reusing a field whose contract says otherwise** — the writer's own section is updated, but the field's other contract (the section its readers obey) is not, so the two disagree and readers mislabel the new values — `example: e84e42d feat(shim): price receipts for upstreams that bill outside the response (#34)`.
- **A ported normalizer whose search string equals its replacement** — a `\u003e` decoded to `>` on both sides of a `strings.NewReplacer`, so the escape it names is never replaced and the comparison that needs it silently fails — `example: e2b3c4d feat(core): Go ports of settings-compose, model-window, context-probe (#36 step 2)`.
- **A deadline only cooperative checks enforce** — the context is tested between steps while a blocking call (a `Flock`, a subprocess, a context-free read) waits past it — `example: e2b3c4d feat(core): Go ports of settings-compose, model-window, context-probe (#36 step 2)`; 2026-11-13: #482 rebuilt `runningAdapter`'s one-second bound as a goroutine plus a `select`, so the bound moved from the subprocess to the channel wait and the `ps` it guards — three context-free `exec.Command` calls in util/hop.go — ran past it for the caller's life; the deadline belongs on the subprocess, and the read is cancelled on return (GH-515).
  Seen 1× (2026-11-13).
- **Timer semantics swapped in a port** — urllib's timeout bounded each socket operation, and a single `context.WithTimeout` now bounds the whole exchange, so a slow but flowing transfer fails — `example: e2b3c4d feat(core): Go ports of settings-compose, model-window, context-probe (#36 step 2)`.
- **A per-wait timer that forgets one of the waits it names** — the comment says the timeout bounds connect, first byte and every read, but nothing resets the timer when the headers arrive, so a 0.9s header wait plus a 0.4s first-byte wait fails a 1.2s budget — `example: #66 fix(ctxwindow): the per-wait timeout resets when the headers arrive`.
- **A cleanup gated on a handle its own helper clears first** — the helper clears the route handle, then runs the stop on an already-cancelled context, so the stop never starts and the last-chance cleanup skips because the handle is gone; a provider bridge and its key-bearing `/tmp` config outlive a Ctrl-C — `example: #66 fix(ctxwindow): a Ctrl-C inside a route stop still retires the route`.
- **A path check that forgets a link can sit on a parent directory** — `-e`/`-ef` are true through a carried sidecar dir while the path itself is not a link, so a removal mistakes its own files for native collisions — `example: 93f3db8 fix(profiles): a carried sidecar dir no longer blocks rm`; also `#185 fix(util): a carried sidecar dir gives way before the merge walks it` (2026-11-05: hop planted the sidecar dir as a link at the store path, so the store path resolved to the profile's own inode and the merge deleted the subagent transcripts from both places).
  Seen 1x (2026-11-05).
- **An upgrade deleting a file a running process still references** — a retired helper removed while a live session's route spec still names it, so the next `/model` reads as a gateway failure — `example: #52, b619556 removed libexec/ccmorph-adapter on upgrade under live sessions`.
- **An upgrade changing the argv contract a running launcher still uses** — a util verb's operands or shape changed while a launcher from the previous release, still running a live session, execs the replaced on-disk core on every pass, so the first hop or resume after `ccmorph update` ends the session and consumes its queued switch file — `example: #137 (2026-11-03): 4259525 moved claude-session's env to a file and launch-env's key off the operands, 0224391 cut profile-read and profile-env from five operands to three, none of them still reading the old form; #162 (2026-11-04): 85ea429 (#156) cut config-store, bridge-stop, fetch-listing, project-picker and eight env-carrying verbs a v0.4.6 launcher still execs on the on-disk core, so its next switch exits 2 and its provider bridge outlives the session`.
  Seen 2x (2026-11-03, 2026-11-04).
- **A reader that turns unparseable input into a confident verdict** — a model listing whose `data` is not a list read as "not served" so the carried model is replaced, an unparsed endpoint echoed whole with its userinfo, a redaction cut that cannot tell a path `@` from a userinfo one answering with an invented endpoint instead of none — behind a port-bearing gateway that cut fired whenever the tail behind the `@` parsed as host:port (`https://gw.example.com:8443/v1/@team:8080` → `https://team:8080`, 2026-11-04) — `example: 7487a99 fix(util): model-known answers cannot-tell for a listing whose data is not a list`; also `a59f601 fix(util): redact-url never echoes an endpoint's userinfo`, `#139 fix(profile): a path or query @ names no host (2026-11-03)`, `#164 fix(profile): a path or query @ names no host, whatever the tail (2026-11-04)`. Seen 2× (2026-11-03, 2026-11-04).
- **A diagnostics path that can die instead of degrade** — a panic nothing recovers takes every launch warning with it, since `util.Main` has no recover and the zsh caller drops stderr — `example: 824a001 fix(util): launch diagnostics keep the warnings when the merge raises`; also `#185 fix(util): a walk-time stat failure never reaches a nil FileInfo` (2026-11-05: the discarded `d.Info()` error left a nil FileInfo that `stillUnchanged` dereferenced, killing the core before claude started).
  Seen 1x (2026-11-05).
- **A damage guard not extended to the sibling field the same change added** — the guard counting a damaged cost unpriced sat on `usage.cost` alone, so the same damage in `usage.estimated_cost`, the field that change introduced, took the whole export down where `cost` was survived — `example: #68 fix(export): a damaged estimate is unpriced, never fatal`; also `#185 fix(util): a paste-cache link elsewhere merges like projects` (2026-11-05: `paste-cache` joined `projects` in `sharedDirs`, but the link-elsewhere exemption and the unreachable-store tolerance were extended only to `projects`).
  Seen 1x (2026-11-05).
- **A value filter that rejects the very values it exists to catch** — an all-letter labeled password read as a code identifier, so `DB_PASSWORD=changeme` goes upstream in the clear (2026-11-05: the prose guard #174 added refused to learn an all-letter value whenever a word follows it, so `DB_PASSWORD=hunterstable DEBUG=1`, an .env dump on one line, went upstream in the clear while the same value at end of line was masked) — `example: #64 fix(shim): a labeled all-letter password is a value, not a code identifier`; also `#186 fix(shim): an .env dump on one line is assignments, not prose (2026-11-05)`, `#215 fix(shim): a URL's password is masked however it is spelled (2026-11-07: the unsure gate #213 added and #214 broadened ran for every rule with a capture group, so the prefix it read as a label was the URL rule's username — postgres://app:, https://client_id: — and a password of letters and dashes, or any password behind a name-like username, went upstream in the clear while the same value with a digit in it stayed masked)`. Seen 3× (2026-10-30, 2026-11-05, 2026-11-07).
- **A length floor counted in bytes where the contract says characters** — two CJK characters pass a six floor, so 密码 is learned and replaced in ordinary prose — `example: #64 fix(shim): the six-value floor counts characters, not bytes`.
- **A stream restorer that skips the final unterminated event** — a stream cut right after a complete `data:` line forwards that line's placeholder to the client — `example: #64 fix(shim): a cut reply stream still restores its final event`.
- **A held join flushed by an unrelated event** — a `ping` between the two halves of a split placeholder breaks the join and the literal placeholder reaches the client — `example: #64 fix(shim): a ping between two halves of a placeholder does not break the join`.
- **A masker that descends deeper than its restorer** — a thinking-shaped object nested in a tool_use input keeps its placeholder, so the tool receives the placeholder instead of the value — `example: #64 fix(shim): the restorer descends tool input as deep as the masker`.
- **A secret file created empty and filled by a second call** — a racing or crashed first launch leaves a zero-byte key file every later launch refuses until it is deleted by hand — `example: #64 fix(shim): a mask key file holds the whole key or none`.
- **A keychain lookup by service alone where the service is shared across items** — `ccmorph quota` reads another account's item or reports "not signed in" for a signed-in profile — `example: #64 fix(quota): the keychain lookup names the account, not just the service`.
- **A byte stripped by one reader and saved back by another writer of the same file** — the BOM dropped where settings.json is parsed, then saved raw into `cache/settings.base.json`, which every later launch re-reads, so one accepted launch failed all the ones after it until a cache file the user never edited was deleted by hand — `example: #67 fix(core): a BOM never reaches the saved copy every later launch re-reads`.
- **A confident verdict kept for a shape the sibling fix already made uncertain** — a listing whose `data` is not a list was made cannot-tell, but a reply whose top level was not an object still answered not-served, so the same unfamiliar reply kept replacing the carried model — `example: #67 fix(util): model-known answers cannot-tell for a listing whose top level is not a JSON object`.
- **A fallback home that only some path builders use** (2026-11-03) — with `HOME` unset the state dir and the context policy took the account's home from the passwd entry, while the canonical settings, the projects stores, doctor, rm and setup-profile still joined `os.Getenv("HOME")`, so a `.claude/settings.json` in the current directory set the launch's model — `example: #138 fix(launch): with HOME unset every reader uses the account's home`.
  Seen 1x (2026-11-03).
- **A fixture whose mode the runner's umask can mask away** — the 0644 file a refusal fixture writes lands 0600 under a private umask, so the refusal the test exists to pin never happens and the suite fails for the environment, not the code; the same change's 0600 session env file had only defers behind it, which the signal path's os.Exit skips, so a TERM between writing it and starting claude left the credentials with no sweep (2026-11-03) — `example: #142 fix(util): the refusal fixture pins its mode, and gc-stale sweeps ccmorph-session-env.*`.
  Seen 1x (2026-11-03).
- **A drop-in replacement that ships without the test pinning the old contract** (2026-11-04) — a hand-written decoder was swapped for the standard library's and its pins were deleted with it, so nothing failed when the new one rewrote a lone-surrogate escape in `.claude.json` to U+FFFD, accepted invalid UTF-8 as U+FFFD, let U+001C-U+001F into the store where the context reader drops them, compared distinct integers above 2^53 equal, and printed `[Errno N]` in the unreachable note; #48's fix was undone in the same change that removed its tests — `example: #163 (bd34df7 and 30ef115 dropped pycompat and its pins; the deleted pins are back in ordjson, util and settingscompose)`.
  Seen 1x (2026-11-04).
- **A fixed-port test drawing its number from the ephemeral pool every parallel gate process draws from** (2026-11-05) — the port came from a bind-to-zero draw, so the number is one the OS hands out of its ephemeral range to any worker's listener, shim or outbound connection (a number released by the draw is free for whoever draws next, and a number held on one address does not stop the OS handing it out on another), and between the draw and the test's subject binding that port a parallel process can take it, so a full gate fails a test that is green alone; the draw belongs below every range's floor — 1024-32767, under macOS's 49152 and Linux's 32768, where no bind-to-zero can land, the fixed services that live down there skipped — `example: 8b9cce5 test(adapter): the listener on another address takes a port no worker can draw (#176)`; also `#188 test: every fixed-port draw leaves the ephemeral pool the gate races on` (2026-11-05: #176's fix covered the one test it saw; the free_port()-based fixed-port tests kept a narrower window of the same race, the residue noted the same day).

- **A busy check sampled before the racer it guards against can register** (2026-11-05) — setup sampled `liveSessions` once right after a non-blocking setup lock, while the launch that lost that lock still started claude; a winner that sampled before the loser wrote `sessions/<pid>.json` merged and swapped `projects` under it — `example: #185 fix(util): a launch holds the profile's live lock for its session`; and the lock that fix added was lost, never taken, or held for the wrong session: Linux flock(2) drops a shared lock before it tries an upgrade, so a failed SH→EX upgrade left the launch with none; a launch that outlasted its wait on a stuck exclusive holder discarded `HoldLive`'s nil and started claude unlocked; and the launcher kept the hopped-away profile's lock for its whole life, so another launch of that profile deferred its merges through the hopped session — `#205 fix(util): a failed upgrade keeps the launch's live lock`, `#205 fix(cli): a launch without its live lock does not start` (2026-11-06), `#205 fix(cli): a hop releases the live lock of the profile it leaves` (2026-11-06).

- **A sweep that deletes what its walk failed to see** (2026-11-06) — the walk's callback skipped an errored subtree without counting it, so the `kept == 0` RemoveAll that followed took parked transcripts that existed nowhere else, once a stalled volume answered the walk with an error and recovered before the sweep; a sweep removes only what its walk named or what is provably empty, and a test of one must make the read fail and then recover, since RemoveAll cannot enter a dir chmod left unreadable either — `example: #204 fix(util): a park sweep removes only the dirs left empty`.

- **Evidence consumed before the decision that needs it, beside a tail window that can skip the line that matters** (2026-11-09) — the Remote Control supervisor marked a host's logs read before its 10-minute login-restart cooldown check, so the failure line it deferred on was gone when the window closed and a host that lost its login again inside the cooldown was never restarted; and its login reader looked only at the last 64 KB of each log, so a verbose session that buried its own failure line under later output was never seen. Consume evidence only once the decision it serves is made, read everything a run printed since the last look, and never step past a line the writer has not finished — Example: 5cf8680 (2026-11-09).

- **A verdict line reports ready without testing the thing it vouches for** — the report's last line is a promise: `OK ready` says the profile will start, so a check that prints a neutral line — an INFO naming what launch does — and leaves the verdict green has passed nothing; the verdict inherited confidence from a line that never asked the question, and whatever a report vouches for, it either tests it or says it was not checked. The gap hides best one branch over from a check that was just added: the sibling branch reads as coverage — `example: 41be89c (2026-11-09) fix(doctor): the report ends with whether the profile is ready (#231), which tested only the API-key branch, so a sub or token profile on Anthropic's own endpoint kept a ready verdict with its credential never tested`. 2026-11-10: #412 doctor asked the adapter about a gateway profile's saved model spelling while launch translates it through model_map before classifying it, so a model the listing declares as needing the translator got no adapter row and the profile kept its ready verdict; also `#411 fix(doctor): a mask value the shim refuses fails the verdict (2026-11-10)`, where the same flag the shim refuses was read only for whether it turned masking on, so doctor printed no masking row and kept the verdict ready until the launch died in the shim; 2026-11-12: #412's fix covered model_map translation only; a tier-word saved model is resolved by launch before classification, and doctor still asked about the tier word, so a chat-dialect id behind a tier alias kept its ready verdict with no adapter row.
  Seen 4× (2026-11-09, 2026-11-10, 2026-11-12).
- **A stop recorded without waiting for the process to be gone** (2026-11-09) — the Remote Control supervisor sent an orphaned host one SIGINT and recorded the restart, its retry time and the cooldown at once: no deadline, no SIGTERM or SIGKILL, no check that the pid had exited, so a host that ignored SIGINT kept its port and kept serving while the cooldown said it was replaced and nothing tried again. A stop waits a bounded time for the pid to be gone, escalates SIGINT → SIGTERM → SIGKILL, and records only a confirmed exit; one that survives is retried — Example: 91eed07 (2026-11-09).
  Seen 1× (2026-11-09).
- **A two-step migration that ignores the failure between its steps while its readers trust it** (2026-11-09) — the one-time move of flat usage rows into day folders linked each row into its day folder and then removed the flat name with the remove's error dropped, so a crash between the two or a remove that failed left the row under both names; a re-run met the day name as taken (EEXIST) and kept the flat copy forever, and the report and the quota, trusting the move to leave each row in one place, summed both copies on every run. A step that can stop halfway is finished or undone by the next run (a taken name that is a second name for this very file is the earlier run's claim, not another row's), every step's error is checked, and a reader that spans the old and the new store counts a row once by its identity — Example: 1304cf1 (2026-11-09).
  Seen 1× (2026-11-09).
- **A refusal that names the cause but not the repair its channel promises** (2026-11-10) — the line is the whole message on a channel that passes it through untouched, so one that stops at the cause leaves the person holding it: 2026-11-10: #375's message-refusal EXIT carried the gateway's own words with no repair, while the REFUSED contract says the launcher adds nothing because the line is the whole message, though every sibling refusal ends with the one command that repairs or diagnoses it — Example: #448 fix(adapter): a gateway's message refusal ends with its repair.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-10).
- **One table of a set gaining an entry the others miss** (2026-11-10) — `profile` joined ownVerbs and its help page when the verb arrived (#275), but neither verbArity nor realVerbs, so `ccmorph profile --help` answered `ccmorph: usage: ccmorph profile` with exit 2 and a mistyped `profil` was offered no command; a verb that joins one table joins them all, and every table's own surface is tested when a verb arrives — `example: #413 fix(cli): the profile verb joins the arity and typo-hint tables`.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-10).
- **A wrapper that names its neighbour from the link's directory instead of the script's** (2026-11-10) — a launcher reached through a symlink took `dirname "$0"` as where it lived, so the program it execs was joined beside the link and the command died with no such file; follow the link chain to the script before building the path to what ships beside it — `example: #416 fix(scripts): the usage-export wrapper follows a link before naming its neighbour (2026-11-10)`.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-10).
- **A formatter's drift the gate never runs** (2026-11-10) — `gofmt -l` named `cli/inspect.go` and `shim/shim_test.go` on main while CI built and tested every Go package and ran no formatter, so drift an editor reports at once landed silently and stayed: the inspect line came in with #360's wording change (e6d2bb4, 2026-11-09), the shim test table was older, and nothing on the gate named either until a hand-run on 2026-11-10. A formatter the repo standardises on is a step in the gate, so a branch whose `gofmt -l` is non-empty fails before its build — `example: #420 ci: the gate fails on gofmt drift`.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-10).
- **A test whose lens reaches outside the tree it guards** (2026-11-10) — the #303 dedup guard walked the checkout directory for every `.go` file, so a sibling session's private worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, code in flight that still carried the helper the guard forbids, failed it on main on 2026-11-10, naming a file this tree does not ship. A guard's walk skips a directory only when git itself says it is another tree: the repository registers it (`git worktree list`) and git run inside it finds its top level there. A `.git` entry alone proves nothing — an empty file, an empty directory, a gitfile pointing nowhere or a repository of its own marks no sibling — and a tracked file is the tree's wherever it lies; skipping at any `.git` entry, or narrowing the walk to git's tracked or non-ignored files, loses copies the walk caught, which is lost coverage, not a fix. Its regression test adds a real worktree with `git worktree add`, puts a hand-written copy in it and asserts the guard stays green, while a copy the tree holds — tracked, untracked or ignored, beside a stray `.git`, or in a worktree git can no longer open — still fails it — `example: #415 test(guard): the dedup guard stops at a sibling worktree's root`.
  Seen 1× (2026-11-10).

## Gate rules

A kind the Hive hit on three different days stops being a description of what
failure looks like and becomes a rule: a diff that breaks one is refused, naming
its kind.

- **An override one reader honours and another forgets** — the runtime derives a path from an env override while a second reader of the same path hardcodes the default, or answers the same question about strings where the first answers it about directories, so the two disagree about where a thing lives: `install.sh --uninstall` kept naming `~/.config/ccmorph` as the profiles' home on a host whose `CCMORPH_STATE_DIR` had moved them, and never named the redirected root — `example: #143 fix(install): uninstall names the state root CCMORPH_STATE_DIR selects`; and the reader that fix wrote forgot the override moves nothing, so on a host that set it after the profiles already lived in `~/.config/ccmorph` it counted only the redirected root, named the code dir as the installed code alone, read no keychain refs from it and offered it on the rm line, and following the printed cleanup deleted the profiles — `#165 fix(install): uninstall names the pre-override profiles CONFIG_DIR still holds` (2026-11-04); and the report that fix wrote named the config dir for deletion while the plugin-index repair still ran for the redirected root alone, so following the printed cleanup deleted plugin files `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` still pointed at and native claude could not load them, and it answered "was it redirected?" by comparing the roots as strings, so a `CCMORPH_STATE_DIR` that spelled the config dir with a trailing slash or through a symlink printed the same profiles, keychain refs and rm targets twice — and the fix's first cut still handed rm the override's own spelling, so a state root that was itself a symlink was removed as a link and the directory it named, with every profile in it, stayed behind — `#187 fix(install): uninstall repairs the plugin index the pre-override profiles still spell` (2026-11-05); and that fix enforced its own requirement only when the two roots were one directory, and there with the config dir unresolved, so a redirected state root that was a symlink, or a config dir that was one, still reached the rm line as the link, and following the printed cleanup left the profiles, credentials and session history at the target, removed as a link and named nowhere — `#207 fix(install): uninstall's rm line names the directory a link leads to` (2026-11-06).
  Seen 4x (2026-11-03, 2026-11-04, 2026-11-05, 2026-11-06).
- **A fallback home for private data that no sweeper owns** (2026-11-04) — the #140 fallback put a private session's view under the state root's run/ when TMPDIR cannot be written, a root the #142 sweep had covered for env files only, so a core killed with SIGKILL left the session's real transcripts, history and shell snapshots in a directory the OS never cleans, with the defer the kill skips as the only remover (2026-11-04: the killed session's view sat under run/ with nothing naming or reaping it); a fallback home for private data lands with the sweep that reaps it, and that sweep gates on the process that uses the data — claude itself, which can outlive both the helper and the machine — never on the helper whose defer a kill skips, and on that process's identity, never on its number alone: the OS hands a dead pid's number to a later same-user process that answers kill(pid, 0) just the same, so the check must ask whether the process holding the number is the one the record names — one that started no later than the record of it — and a pid it cannot read it keeps (2026-11-05: the #166 sweep asked kill alone, so a recycled pid kept the killed session's view out of the sweep indefinitely); and identity is never a word in the pid's command line: the #189 check accepted claude anywhere in its argv, so a `grep -r claude ~/notes`, an editor on a claude.md or another Claude Code session holding the recycled number kept a dead session's transcripts, history and shell snapshots on disk, and the relay sweep in the same function still asked kill(pid, 0) alone, so a recycled launcher pid kept a stale .reswitch relay out of the sweep for good (2026-11-06); and identity is never a clock's verdict either: the #206 check read the record's mtime, a filesystem's clock (the root holding the view, a state root or a tmp that can sit on another host's), against the kernel's start time, and nothing keeps the two in step, so a state or tmp filesystem whose timestamps lagged by more than its minute, or a Linux host whose wall clock stepped backward after boot (ps lstart is boot-relative), made a live claude read as a recycled pid, and the sweep deleted the live session's real transcripts, history and shell snapshots; widening the window kept recycled pids' views, and a probe that measured the filesystem's lag at sweep time missed a step and a lag since corrected, so identity is the kernel's own start mark, read when claude starts and kept beside the record, which no clock moves, and a record without one keeps kill alone (2026-11-07) — `example: #166 fix(util): gc-stale reaps the private views a killed session leaves`; also `#189 fix(util): gc-stale reaps the private view a recycled pid spares`; and `#206 fix(util): gc-stale knows a view's claude by when it started` and `#206 fix(util): gc-stale knows a relay's launcher by when it started` (2026-11-06); and `#218 fix(util): gc-stale knows a view's claude by its start mark, never a clock` (2026-11-07).
  Seen 4x (2026-11-04, 2026-11-05, 2026-11-06, 2026-11-07).
- **A suite green on the gate and red on a machine that carries the real tool** (2026-11-10) — the test env filtered the picker's fzf from PATH but left cliproxyapi, and the Go core reads the add menu's provider rows from that bridge, so the machine's own longer Kimi logins widened the label column and the two tests pinning the Claude row's padding failed only where the bridge was installed; the gate has none, so the change landed green and stayed green while a real machine failed. A test env hides every tool its subject shells out to, and a test that needs one writes its own stub — `example: #414 fix(picker): a test env hides the provider bridge, not only fzf` (2026-11-10); and the hiding that fix wrote dropped every PATH entry carrying the bridge whole, so a machine keeping it beside its other tools — a merged-/usr Linux with jq and even zsh in the same /usr/bin — lost them from every test home, and what a test then resolved depended on where that machine kept its tools, while the gate, carrying no bridge, dropped nothing and stayed green: a tool is hidden by name, its entry mirrored, never dropped whole — `#476 fix(tests): a bridge-carrying PATH entry is mirrored, not dropped` (2026-11-12).
  Seen 2× (2026-11-10, 2026-11-12).

## Never blocks

Style, naming, wording, formatting, and "could be cleaner" go in the PR as notes,
at most 3 per review; drop the rest. A pre-existing bug the diff did not
introduce is a new issue, not a finding.

## Where the rules live

Scope, high-risk classes and the `_ccm_launch -a` contract are in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md); test homes and the Verification suites are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); the integration boundaries are in
[ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#scope-and-ownership). Check the diff
against them, do not restate them.
